editor_note: All six rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. The terms are consistent: skill→"kemahiran", AI assistant→"pembantu AI", reusable→"boleh guna semula" and migrating→"memigrasikan". The hedge "Secara umum, anda hanya perlu..." is kept intact.

The meaning holds throughout. The three pre-run checks (entry 9), the TEM-vs-PEC shot comparison (entry 69) and the function-litar/function-aplikasi split all match the English, and nothing would mislead a learner. What a native editor would still change is a handful of calques. "pre-flight" becomes the literal "pra-penerbangan", "back-test" becomes the coined "menguji-belakang", and "out of the box" becomes the odd "secara terus pakai". The relative clause "with which users can" is rendered with the English-style "di mana" (entries 68 and 72), and "pipelines" is the bare "paip" (entry 18).

examples.source: New pre-flight checks
examples.translation: Semakan pra-penerbangan baharu
examples.suggested: Semakan pra-larian baharu
examples.why: 'pra-penerbangan' is a literal aviation calque. In this context the checks run before a job, so 'pra-larian' (or 'semakan awal sebelum larian') reads naturally.

examples.source: to back-test portfolio optimization strategies
examples.translation: menguji-belakang strategi pengoptimuman portfolio
examples.suggested: melakukan ujian balik (back-test) strategi pengoptimuman portfolio
examples.why: 'menguji-belakang' is a coined hyphenated calque. Malay finance writing uses 'ujian balik', or keeps 'back-test'.

examples.source: to make utility-grade performance accessible out of the box
examples.translation: untuk menjadikan prestasi gred utiliti boleh diakses secara terus pakai
examples.suggested: supaya prestasi gred utiliti boleh dicapai terus tanpa konfigurasi tambahan
examples.why: 'secara terus pakai' is a stiff rendering of the idiom 'out of the box'.

examples.source: with which users can scale successfully to larger problems
examples.translation: di mana pengguna boleh berskala dengan berjaya kepada masalah yang lebih besar
examples.suggested: yang membolehkan pengguna berjaya menskalakan penyelesaian kepada masalah yang lebih besar
examples.why: Using 'di mana' as a relative pronoun is an English calque, and entry 72 repeats it. 'berskala dengan berjaya' is also stiff.

examples.source: Fail fast in pipelines and notebooks
examples.translation: Gagal dengan cepat dalam paip dan buku nota
examples.suggested: Gagal awal dalam saluran paip (pipeline) dan buku nota
examples.why: The bare 'paip' reads as a physical pipe. The usual software term is 'saluran paip', or 'pipeline' kept in English.

editor_note: Entry [287] reverses the deprecation deadline. "will be removed no sooner than 30 September 2024" is rendered "tidak lewat daripada", which means "no later than", so a reader would think optimization_level could disappear any day before that date, which is wrong. Several smaller slips don't mislead: [168] drops "later" from "later this year", and [221] renders "Deprecation" as "penyahtauliahan" (decommissioning), a term the file otherwise uses for retiring QPUs. Terms are also inconsistent: "fidelity" appears as fideliti [8], ketepatan [178] and the too-literal kesetiaan [110], and "collaborators" as "Pekerja bersama" [124] and "kolaborator" [239].

examples.source: will be removed no sooner than 30 September 2024
examples.translation: akan dialih keluar tidak lewat daripada 30 September 2024
examples.suggested: akan dialih keluar tidak lebih awal daripada 30 September 2024
examples.why: Reverses the meaning. The English says removal happens on this date or later, but the Malay says on this date or earlier.

examples.source: Additional features will be rolled out later this year.
examples.translation: Ciri tambahan akan dilancarkan pada tahun ini.
examples.suggested: Ciri tambahan akan dilancarkan kemudian pada tahun ini.
examples.why: Drops 'later', which tells the reader these features are not available yet.

examples.source: Deprecation reminder: The deprecation date for IBM Quantum Platform Classic
examples.translation: Peringatan penyahtauliahan: Tarikh penyahtauliahan
examples.suggested: Peringatan penamatan: Tarikh penamatan
examples.why: The file uses 'penyahtauliahan' for retiring hardware and 'dinyahkegunakan' for deprecation. Here the two are mixed up for a platform sunset.

examples.source: it might improve the fidelity of certain circuits
examples.translation: ia mungkin meningkatkan kesetiaan litar tertentu
examples.suggested: ia mungkin meningkatkan fideliti litar tertentu
examples.why: 'kesetiaan' means loyalty. The same file uses 'fideliti' in [8] and 'ketepatan' in [178].

examples.source: Collaborators retain access to results
examples.translation: Pekerja bersama mengekalkan akses kepada hasil
examples.suggested: Kolaborator mengekalkan akses kepada hasil
examples.why: The same role is 'kolaborator' in [239]. 'Pekerja bersama' is a stiff calque.

editor_note: Entry 21 is faithful: "Salin dan simpan token pembawa yang dikembalikan" and "menyertakan CRN dan token pembawa dalam pengepala permintaan" keep the English meaning, and "bearer token" is rendered as "token pembawa", matching entry [20].

Neither rewritten entry would mislead a learner. Entry 30 follows the English symbol by symbol, including the source's own stress/strain labelling, with correct terms (modulus pukal, had tegasan berkadar, terikan). Entry 16 renders "initial condition" two ways in back-to-back sentences: "keadaan awal" first, then "syarat awal". It also uses "cecair" (liquid) for "fluid", while entry 18 uses the more accurate "bendalir". "Relax" as "mencapai keseimbangan" is a defensible reading, but "berevolusi"/"menyesuaikan diri" would stay closer to the source.

examples.source: you can select the initial condition ... the only accepted initial conditions are linear functions
examples.translation: anda boleh memilih keadaan awal ... satu-satunya syarat awal yang diterima
examples.suggested: anda boleh memilih syarat awal ... satu-satunya syarat awal yang diterima
examples.why: The same term, 'initial condition', gets two renderings within one entry. 'syarat awal' matches 'syarat sempadan' and entries 45/48.

examples.source: $u$ represents the fluid speed field
examples.translation: $u$ mewakili medan kelajuan cecair
examples.suggested: $u$ mewakili medan kelajuan bendalir
examples.why: 'cecair' means liquid, while the standard physics term for 'fluid' is 'bendalir', which entry 18 already uses. This is a minor narrowing and inconsistency.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The 90%/80% mitigation thresholds in [31]-[33], the caution in [25] that the Aer noise model is likely less severe than real QPU noise, and the to_clifford caveat in [18] (it does not change two-qubit gates, qubit count or depth) all match the English. A native editor would still fix a few things. 'Initialize' is rendered as 'mulakan'/'memulakan', which gives the redundant 'Mula-mula, mulakan `Neat`' in [19] and the vague 'Mulakan Circuit sasaran' in [11]. 'Primitive unified blocs' becomes 'blok kesatuan primitif' in [16], where 'kesatuan' means 'union', not 'unified'. 'Figure of merit' is calqued as 'angka merit' in [24] and [28].

examples.source: First, initialize `Neat`.
examples.translation: Mula-mula, mulakan `Neat`.
examples.suggested: Mula-mula, inisialisasikan `Neat`.
examples.why: 'Mula-mula, mulakan' repeats the same root, which reads as clumsy. 'Mulakan' also means 'start', not 'initialize an object'.

examples.source: use them to initialize the primitive unified blocs (PUBs)
examples.translation: gunakannya untuk memulakan blok kesatuan primitif (PUB)
examples.suggested: gunakannya untuk membina blok bersatu primitif (PUB)
examples.why: 'Kesatuan' means 'union/association', not 'unified'. 'Memulakan' (start) is a weak rendering of 'initialize' when the sense is 'construct'.

examples.source: to calculate figures of merit
examples.translation: untuk mengira angka merit
examples.suggested: untuk mengira metrik prestasi
examples.why: 'Angka merit' is a word-for-word calque of 'figure of merit'. A Malay technical writer would more likely use 'metrik prestasi' or 'ukuran prestasi'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and core terms stay consistent: pengurangan ralat for mitigation, penindasan ralat for suppression, tahap daya tahan for resilience level and hingar for noise. A native editor would still change four things. "Trade-off" is rendered as "pertukaran kos/ketepatan", which reads as "exchange" rather than "compromise"; "tolak ansur" is better. "On a rolling basis" becomes "secara bergilir" ("taking turns"), when "secara berperingkat" is meant. "Measurement mitigation" is shortened to "pengurangan ukuran", which is ambiguous; "pengurangan ralat pengukuran" is clearer. Finally, the table's statistical "estimators" is capitalized as the Estimator primitive.

examples.source: to configure the cost/accuracy trade-off
examples.translation: mengkonfigurasi pertukaran kos/ketepatan
examples.suggested: mengkonfigurasi tolak ansur kos/ketepatan
examples.why: 'pertukaran' means exchange/swap. The idiomatic Malay for trade-off is 'tolak ansur' (or 'keseimbangan'). The same issue is in [18] 'pertukaran masa-ketepatan'.

examples.source: will be released on a rolling basis
examples.translation: akan dikeluarkan secara bergilir
examples.suggested: akan dikeluarkan secara berperingkat
examples.why: 'bergilir' means taking turns or rotating. 'Rolling basis' means incremental releases over time.

examples.source: but then turn off measurement mitigation
examples.translation: tetapi kemudian mematikan pengurangan ukuran
examples.suggested: tetapi kemudian mematikan pengurangan ralat pengukuran
examples.why: 'pengurangan ukuran' can read as 'reduction of size/measurement'. Measurement-error mitigation (TREX) should be named explicitly.

examples.source: Typically reduces bias in estimators
examples.translation: Biasanya mengurangkan berat sebelah dalam Estimator
examples.suggested: Biasanya mengurangkan berat sebelah dalam penganggar
examples.why: The English lowercase 'estimators' means statistical estimators. The capitalized 'Estimator' suggests the Qiskit primitive.

editor_note: I found no misleading drift. Quantities (1000 randomizations, 11 PUBs, 20,000 shots, batches=4, 26.8 million instructions per qubit) and caveats, such as estimator_options replacing the defaults wholesale, are all kept. A few spots need editing, though. In [62], "circuit instances" becomes "instance Rangkaian" ("network"), which clashes with "Circuit" everywhere else and with "rangkaian tensor" in [31]. Some phrases are calques: "dikira ke arahnya" for "count toward it" in [60], "Kipaskan" for "fan … across" in [39], and "Berkembang"/"untuk berkembang" (grow) for time evolution in [39], where "evolusi"/"berevolusi" would be clearer.

examples.line_approx: lebih kurang satu persepuluh daripada instance Rangkaian
examples.source: about a tenth of the circuit instances the defaults would submit
examples.translation: lebih kurang satu persepuluh daripada instance Rangkaian yang akan dihantar oleh lalai
examples.suggested: lebih kurang satu persepuluh daripada instance Circuit yang akan dihantar oleh lalai
examples.why: 'Rangkaian' means network. Everywhere else the file uses 'Circuit', and 'rangkaian tensor' in [31] refers to tensor networks, so this line swaps in a different concept.

examples.line_approx: menambah Gate yang dikira ke arahnya
examples.source: Dynamical decoupling adds gates that count toward it.
examples.translation: Penyahgandingan dinamik menambah Gate yang dikira ke arahnya.
examples.suggested: Penyahgandingan dinamik menambah Gate yang turut dikira dalam had tersebut.
examples.why: 'ke arahnya' (toward its direction) is a literal calque of 'count toward'. It does not make clear that these gates count against the instruction limit.

examples.source: Evolves to `T = t_steps * dt` ... A prepared `QuantumCircuit` to evolve.
examples.translation: Berkembang kepada `T = t_steps * dt` ... `QuantumCircuit` yang disediakan untuk berkembang.
examples.suggested: Berevolusi hingga `T = t_steps * dt` ... `QuantumCircuit` yang disediakan untuk dievolusikan.
examples.why: 'Berkembang' means grow or develop, not time evolution. The rest of the file already uses 'evolusi masa'.

examples.source: Fan the local simulator paths across all available cores with Ray.
examples.translation: Kipaskan laluan simulator tempatan merentasi semua teras yang tersedia dengan Ray.
examples.suggested: Agihkan laluan simulator tempatan merentasi semua teras yang tersedia menggunakan Ray.
examples.why: 'Kipaskan' (to fan, as with a fan) is a word-for-word calque of 'fan out' and does not read as natural Malay.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing would mislead a learner. The Executor/directed-execution description, the template-circuit/samplex explanation and the 25-shot setup all match the English. There are three small problems. Entry [16] switches to casual "Kamu" when the rest of the file uses "anda". Entry [20] has the misspelling "ditransail" where [15] correctly uses "transpail" ("ditranspail"). Entry [16]'s "Ia boleh mempunyai parameter secara pilihan" is a stiff calque of "It can optionally have parameters".

examples.source: You need at least one circuit to use the Executor primitive.  It can optionally have parameters.
examples.translation: Kamu memerlukan sekurang-kurangnya satu Circuit untuk menggunakan primitif Executor. Ia boleh mempunyai parameter secara pilihan.
examples.suggested: Anda memerlukan sekurang-kurangnya satu Circuit untuk menggunakan primitif Executor. Circuit ini boleh (tetapi tidak wajib) mempunyai parameter.
examples.why: Uses casual 'Kamu' where the rest of the file uses 'anda'. 'secara pilihan' is a stiff calque of 'optionally'.

examples.source: Next, it appends the transpiled target circuit.
examples.translation: Seterusnya, ia menambahkan Circuit sasaran yang telah ditransail.
examples.suggested: Seterusnya, ia menambahkan Circuit sasaran yang telah ditranspail.
examples.why: 'ditransail' is a misspelling. It doesn't match 'transpail' in entry [15], so the transpile term is spelled inconsistently.

editor_note: Entry 60 keeps the English meaning. Dynamical decoupling is described as error suppression ("penindasan ralat"), resilience level becomes "Tahap ketahanan", and higher levels still give more accurate results but take longer to process. Two small fixes are worth making. "dengan mengorbankan masa pemprosesan yang lebih lama" is a calque of "at the expense of" and literally says you sacrifice the longer processing time, which reads awkwardly. The link text "Error mitigation and suppression techniques" is left in English, although other guide link titles on the page are translated (e.g. "Pasang Qiskit", "Simpan kelayakan log masuk anda").

examples.source: Higher levels generate more accurate results, at the expense of longer processing times.
examples.translation: Tahap yang lebih tinggi menghasilkan keputusan yang lebih tepat, dengan mengorbankan masa pemprosesan yang lebih lama.
examples.suggested: Tahap yang lebih tinggi menghasilkan keputusan yang lebih tepat, tetapi memerlukan masa pemprosesan yang lebih lama.
examples.why: This calques 'at the expense of'. In Malay, 'mengorbankan' plus 'lebih lama' literally means giving up the longer time, which is backwards. A native writer would say the higher levels take more time.

examples.source: see [Error mitigation and suppression techniques](/guides/error-mitigation-and-suppression-techniques)
examples.translation: lihat [Error mitigation and suppression techniques](/guides/error-mitigation-and-suppression-techniques)
examples.suggested: lihat [Teknik mitigasi dan penindasan ralat](/guides/error-mitigation-and-suppression-techniques)
examples.why: The link text is left in English, but other guide link titles on the page are translated, and the same sentence already uses 'penindasan ralat'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and the prerequisites, install command and upgrade advice all match the English. A native editor would still change four things. The page uses casual "kamu" throughout (entries 0, 7, 9, 11) where the convention is "anda". "Deprecation policy" is rendered "dasar penamatan", which reads as "termination policy". "Jobs" is rendered literally as "kerja" rather than "tugas". The spelling "mengemaskini" should be the standard "mengemas kini".

examples.source: Review the [deprecation policy]
examples.translation: Semak [dasar penamatan]
examples.suggested: Semak [dasar penamatan sokongan] (or "dasar deprekasi")
examples.why: 'Penamatan' alone means termination/ending. Deprecation means a feature is marked for future removal, not ended, so the label overstates it slightly.

examples.source: so you can run jobs with IBM Quantum Compute Service
examples.translation: supaya kamu boleh menjalankan kerja dengan IBM Quantum Compute Service
examples.suggested: supaya anda boleh menjalankan tugas (job) dengan IBM Quantum Compute Service
examples.why: The convention is 'anda', not casual 'kamu', and 'kerja' is a literal calque for a computing job. 'Tugas' is the usual technical rendering.

examples.source: We recommend frequently updating your requirements
examples.translation: Kami syorkan agar kamu selalu mengemaskini keperluan
examples.suggested: Kami syorkan agar anda kerap mengemas kini keperluan
examples.why: The standard DBP spelling is 'mengemas kini' (two words), and 'kamu' again breaks the register convention.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep their meaning. Entry 22 keeps every caveat ("boleh bergantung", "dalam sesetengah kes", "mungkin"), and entry 66 keeps ibm_marrakesh, direct_qubit_mapping=True and the 150-node Maxcut run. Entry 22 does not match the terms used on the rest of the page. It uses "instans masalah" where the page says "contoh masalah", "pascapemprosesan" where the page says "pasca-pemprosesan", and "aliran kerja" where the page says "alur kerja" (entries 10, 17, 18). Entry 66 translates "instance" as "contoh", which gives the clumsy "Contoh berikut menjalankan contoh Maxcut" ("the following example runs the Maxcut example"), so a reader cannot tell the code example apart from the benchmark instance.

examples.source: subsequent processing steps ... after equivalent post-processing ... the complete optimization workflow
examples.translation: pascapemprosesan yang setara ... keseluruhan aliran kerja pengoptimuman
examples.suggested: pasca-pemprosesan yang setara ... keseluruhan alur kerja pengoptimuman
examples.why: The rest of the page writes 'pasca-pemprosesan' and 'alur kerja' (entries 10, 16, 17, 18). This rewrite uses different spellings and words for the same terms.

examples.source: the problem instance
examples.translation: instans masalah
examples.suggested: contoh masalah (as in entry 8), or change 'instance' to 'instans' across the whole page
examples.why: Every other entry translates 'instance' as 'contoh' (entries 8, 26-28, 61-63), so this is the only place 'instans' appears.

examples.source: The following example runs the Maxcut instance with 150 nodes.
examples.translation: Contoh berikut menjalankan contoh Maxcut dengan 150 nod.
examples.suggested: Contoh berikut menjalankan instans Maxcut dengan 150 nod.
examples.why: Using 'contoh' for both 'example' and 'instance' makes the sentence read 'the example runs the example', which is awkward and hides the difference between the two.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally. Terms such as "penyedia identiti luaran (IDP)", "log masuk tunggal (SSO)" and "mengesahkan pengguna luaran … secara selamat" are correct, and the caveat "(mungkin dikenakan kos)" and the dynamic-rules tip in [7] keep their meaning.

The meaning is accurate throughout. The deprecation timeline (removed in early 2025, qiskit.pulse deprecated in SDK v1.3.0 and removed in v2.0.0), the requirement that both R_X and R_ZZ be loaded via use_fractional_gates, and the Qiskit Dynamics pointers all come through intact, with a consistent "gate pecahan" / "kawalan peringkat denyutan". The one thing a native editor would change is in entry [5], where "transpilation pipeline" becomes "saluran pengkompilan". That reads as a compilation pipeline and blurs the Qiskit transpile step, which "saluran transpilasi" would name directly. This is imperfect terminology, but it does not mislead.

examples.source: then build a transpilation pipeline containing the calibration builder passes
examples.translation: kemudian membina saluran pengkompilan yang mengandungi laluan pembina penentukuran
examples.suggested: kemudian membina saluran transpilasi yang mengandungi laluan pembina penentukuran
examples.why: 'Pengkompilan' means compilation, not transpilation. The Qiskit-specific transpile step deserves its own conventional term, 'transpilasi'.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, and no negation, quantity or caveat is lost. The caveats "**tidak** dipindahkan" [152] and "Ini bukan pengganti langsung" [115] come through intact. The biggest problem is terminology: transpiler "pass" is translated as "laluan" ([250] heading, [251], [252], and "pengurus laluan" for passmanager in [254]). The file already uses "laluan" for "path" in "laluan import" and "laluan migrasi", so "laluan transpiler" reads as "transpiler path". The other issues are smaller. "observable" becomes "pemerhati" ("observer") in [104] but "observable" in [105]/[76]. "Removed" becomes "Dialih keluar" in [61] but "Dibuang" in every other table. The tab label in [88] says "2 litar" while the neighbouring labels keep "circuits". There are also small slips: "minima" instead of "minimum" in [115], an added "juga" in [37], and "the few changes" becomes "perubahan kecil" in [64].

examples.source: The `NoiseAdaptiveLayout` transpiler pass has been superseded by ... Both the pass and the corresponding `"noise_adaptive"` layout stage plugin have been removed
examples.translation: Laluan transpiler `NoiseAdaptiveLayout` telah digantikan oleh ... Kedua-dua laluan dan plugin peringkat susun atur
examples.suggested: Pass transpiler `NoiseAdaptiveLayout` telah digantikan oleh ... Kedua-dua pass tersebut dan plugin peringkat susun atur
examples.why: 'laluan' means path/route, and this file uses it for 'import path' and 'migration path'. Using it for a transpiler pass mixes up two different concepts. The same fix applies to [250], [252] and [254] ('pengurus laluan').

examples.source: [`Estimator`] observable arguments
examples.translation: argumen pemerhati [`Estimator`]
examples.suggested: argumen observable [`Estimator`]
examples.why: 'pemerhati' means 'observer', which is a different concept. The very next entry [105] and the rest of the file keep 'observable'.

examples.source: Removed | Alternative
examples.translation: Dialih keluar | Alternatif
examples.suggested: Dibuang | Alternatif
examples.why: Every other Removed/Alternative table in the file uses 'Dibuang'.

examples.source: as well as the few changes that have taken place in the inputs accepted by the V1 interface
examples.translation: serta beberapa perubahan kecil yang berlaku pada input yang diterima oleh antara muka V1
examples.suggested: serta beberapa perubahan yang berlaku pada input yang diterima oleh antara muka V1
examples.why: 'few' refers to how many changes there are, not how big they are. Adding 'kecil' (minor) makes the V1 changes sound less important than the source says.

examples.source: but the changes are minimal
examples.translation: tetapi perubahannya adalah minima
examples.suggested: tetapi perubahannya adalah minimum
examples.why: The standard Malay word is 'minimum'. 'minima' is a plural loan form that does not fit here.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The caveats in [13] about the order of PUB execution and batching are kept, and so is the trade-off in [10] where a lower rep_delay means a shorter run but more state-preparation error. A few English-shaped phrases remain. In [10], "dengan mengorbankan peningkatan kadar ralat" copies "at the expense of increasing" word for word and reads as though the increase is what gets given up. In [7], "memperkenalkan ralat" is a calque of "introduce errors". The heading [1] uses "Permulaan Qubit", but "permulaan" means "beginning", not initialization, and the body text in [6] uses "dimulakan" for the same idea.

examples.source: at the expense of increasing the state preparation error rate
examples.translation: dengan mengorbankan peningkatan kadar ralat penyediaan keadaan
examples.suggested: tetapi kadar ralat penyediaan keadaan akan meningkat
examples.why: This copies the English 'at the expense of' structure. Read literally, it says the increase in error is what gets sacrificed, which reverses the intended trade-off. Stating the consequence directly is clearer.

examples.source: imperfections in the reset process can introduce state-preparation errors
examples.translation: ketidaksempurnaan dalam proses set semula boleh memperkenalkan ralat penyediaan keadaan
examples.suggested: ketidaksempurnaan dalam proses set semula boleh menyebabkan ralat penyediaan keadaan
examples.why: 'Memperkenalkan' copies the English 'introduce'. A native technical writer would say 'menyebabkan' (cause).

examples.source: Qubit initialization
examples.translation: Permulaan Qubit
examples.suggested: Pengawalan qubit
examples.why: 'Permulaan' means 'beginning/start', not setting a qubit to its initial state. The word is still recognizable, so this is a minor issue.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the caveats: the stochastic no-guarantee note in [11], the directional ECR gate in [44] and the VF2PostLayout result in [48]. Core terms are consistent: peta gandeng, gate asas, susun atur, penghala, qubit maya/fizikal. A few calqued sentences still read like machine translation. "Ketepatan di mana Transpiler menghasilkan" in [10] copies "precision with which", "menghormati konektiviti" in [36] copies "respects", and the relative clause in [40] ("yang telah dilakukan penentukuran pada QPU") is clumsy. In [6], "anda rancang untuk menghantar kerja" drops the "to" object: the jobs are sent to that object.

examples.source: The precision with which the transpiler produces the most appropriate circuit ... depends on how much information
examples.translation: Ketepatan di mana Transpiler menghasilkan Circuit yang paling sesuai ...
examples.suggested: Sejauh mana Transpiler dapat menghasilkan Circuit yang paling sesuai ... bergantung pada ...
examples.why: 'di mana' is a calque of the English 'with which' and is not natural Malay.

examples.source: Because this layout respects the circuit's connectivity
examples.translation: Kerana susun atur ini menghormati konektiviti Circuit
examples.suggested: Oleh sebab susun atur ini mematuhi konektiviti Circuit
examples.why: 'menghormati' (to honour someone) is a literal rendering of 'respects'. 'mematuhi' or 'sepadan dengan' is the natural technical wording.

examples.source: The default basis gates are those that calibrations have been done for on the QPU
examples.translation: gate asas lalai adalah yang telah dilakukan penentukuran pada QPU
examples.suggested: Gate asas lalai ialah gate yang telah ditentukur pada QPU
examples.why: The relative clause is ungrammatical and hard to read. The sentence also starts in lowercase.

examples.source: the BackendV2 ... object you plan to submit jobs to
examples.translation: objek BackendV2 ... yang anda rancang untuk menghantar kerja
examples.suggested: objek BackendV2 ... yang akan anda gunakan untuk menghantar kerja
examples.why: The sentence loses the target of the jobs: the backend is where the jobs are sent, and the Malay no longer says so.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The IBM/user responsibility split, the "IBM tidak bertanggungjawab" disclaimers and the encryption and backup caveats all match the English, and nothing here would mislead a reader. A native editor would still fix four wording problems. "deployment" is rendered as "penggunaan", which reads as "usage". [17] repeats the verb in "memulihkan dan memulihkan". "Versioning the REST APIs" became "Penomboran" ("numbering") instead of "Pemversian". "Rotate … API keys" is calqued as "Putar".

examples.source: deployment, configuration, upgrades, patching
examples.translation: penggunaan, konfigurasi, naik taraf, tampalan
examples.suggested: pengerahan (atau pelaksanaan), konfigurasi, naik taraf, tampalan
examples.why: 'penggunaan' means usage. In change management it hides the sense of deploying software.

examples.source: Automatically recover and restore IBM Quantum Compute Service capabilities
examples.translation: Secara automatik memulihkan dan memulihkan keupayaan
examples.suggested: Secara automatik memulihkan dan mengembalikan keupayaan
examples.why: The same verb appears twice in a row, which reads as a machine-translation artifact.

examples.source: Versioning the REST APIs.
examples.translation: Penomboran API REST.
examples.suggested: Pemversian API REST.
examples.why: 'Penomboran' means numbering. It is recognizable but less precise than versioning.

examples.source: Rotate and update your API keys
examples.translation: Putar dan kemas kini kunci API anda
examples.suggested: Tukar ganti dan kemas kini kunci API anda
examples.why: 'Putar' is a literal calque of 'rotate'. For key rotation, 'tukar ganti' (or 'gilirkan') is more natural.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the meaning, and neither would mislead a learner. In entry 6, "bergantung kepada kedua-dua PUB yang digunakan serta pilihan runtime" copies the English "both ... as well as" too literally, and "kedua-dua PUB" can be misread as "the two PUBs". Entry 6 also uses singular "Ia" for the plural PUBs. In entry 30, "shots" keeps the English plural -s ("pelaksanaan shots tertentu", "Shots dikumpulkan"), which reads unnaturally in Malay and does not match the bare "shot" used in entry 16 ("data shot yang tersusun").

examples.source: in a format that is dependent on both the PUBs used as well as the runtime options specified from the primitive
examples.translation: dalam format yang bergantung kepada kedua-dua PUB yang digunakan serta pilihan runtime yang ditentukan daripada primitif
examples.suggested: dalam format yang bergantung pada PUB yang digunakan dan juga pilihan runtime yang ditetapkan pada primitif
examples.why: 'kedua-dua PUB' can be read as 'the two PUBs'. It is a literal copy of 'both...as well as', and 'ditentukan daripada primitif' is stiff.

examples.source: when particular shots were executed on the QPU. Shots are grouped into ExecutionSpan objects
examples.translation: pada masa pelaksanaan shots tertentu pada QPU. Shots dikumpulkan ke dalam objek ExecutionSpan
examples.suggested: pada masa pelaksanaan shot tertentu pada QPU. Shot dikumpulkan ke dalam objek ExecutionSpan
examples.why: Malay does not add a plural -s to borrowed terms, and entry 16 uses the bare 'shot', so the file is inconsistent.

editor_note: One sentence gets the meaning backwards. In [80], "Heron processors with ~10× improved error rates" becomes "~10× peningkatan kadar ralat", which most Malay readers will take as a tenfold increase in errors, so the IBM hardware strengths paragraph ends up making a negative claim. The other problems are minor. "Error mitigation" is translated two ways ("pengurangan ralat" in [34], "mitigasi ralat" in [47]). Gate fidelity is the literal "kesetiaan gate", which reads as "loyalty", in [38]. Coherence time is "masa koheren", missing the final "s" of "koherens" [37]. In [48], "allow for experimentation" is calqued as "membolehkan eksperimen" ("enable experimentation") when it means "take into account", and "kamu" slips in for "anda" in [40], [43] and [48].

examples.source: built around Heron processors with ~10× improved error rates
examples.translation: dibina sekitar pemproses Heron dengan ~10× peningkatan kadar ralat
examples.suggested: dibina sekitar pemproses Heron dengan kadar ralat ~10× lebih rendah
examples.why: 'Peningkatan kadar ralat' most naturally means 'an increase in error rate', so a learner would read that Heron has ten times more errors, the opposite of the source.

examples.source: When we allow for experimentation, benchmarking of your problem, and multiple attempts, this time range is consistent with the aforementioned minimum.
examples.translation: Apabila kita membolehkan eksperimen, penanda aras masalah anda, dan pelbagai percubaan, julat masa ini konsisten dengan minimum yang disebutkan di atas.
examples.suggested: Apabila kita mengambil kira eksperimen, penanda aras masalah anda dan beberapa percubaan, julat masa ini selaras dengan minimum yang disebutkan di atas.
examples.why: 'Allow for' means 'take into account', not 'enable'. The calque blurs why 30-120 minute runs add up to the 400-minute minimum.

examples.source: They have high gate fidelity
examples.translation: Mereka mempunyai kesetiaan gate yang tinggi
examples.suggested: Ia mempunyai fideliti get yang tinggi
examples.why: 'Kesetiaan' means loyalty. The technical term is 'fideliti'. 'Mereka' (a pronoun for people) is also used for qubits.

examples.source: outline your intended use of literal error mitigation strategies
examples.translation: menggariskan penggunaan strategi pengurangan ralat literal yang anda inginkan
examples.suggested: menggariskan strategi mitigasi ralat yang anda rancang untuk gunakan
examples.why: Entry [47] uses 'mitigasi ralat' for error mitigation, so the term is inconsistent within the file. The source also contrasts general project 'mitigation' with literal error mitigation, and that contrast is clearer with the technical term.

examples.source: You might focus on the scale and accessibility of quantum computers
examples.translation: Kamu mungkin menumpukan pada skala dan kebolehaksesan komputer kuantum
examples.suggested: Anda mungkin menumpukan pada skala dan kebolehaksesan komputer kuantum
examples.why: Casual 'kamu' breaks the 'anda' convention used in the rest of the file. It also appears in [43] and [48].

editor_note: The translation is faithful overall, and nothing in it would mislead a learner. There are four small slips. In [5], "there's little doubt" becomes "tidak ada keraguan" ("there is no doubt"), which makes the claim slightly stronger than the English. In [6], "discretization of errors" is rendered "pendigitan ralat" ("digitization"), when "pendiskretan ralat" would match the source term more precisely. In [4], "persekitaran sekitar" repeats itself, and "secara melampau" suggests "excessively" rather than "to an extreme degree".

examples.source: Today, there's little doubt that building ... is a monumental challenge.
examples.translation: Hari ini, tidak ada keraguan bahawa membina ...
examples.suggested: Hari ini, hampir tiada keraguan bahawa membina ...
examples.why: 'little doubt' is a hedge; 'tidak ada keraguan' removes it and strengthens the claim slightly.

examples.source: discretization of errors
examples.translation: pendigitan ralat
examples.suggested: pendiskretan ralat
examples.why: The course's named concept is discretization; 'pendigitan' (digitization) is recognizable but less precise.

examples.source: isolate the quantum information they store from the environment around them to an extreme degree
examples.translation: mengasingkan maklumat kuantum yang disimpannya daripada persekitaran sekitar secara melampau
examples.suggested: mengasingkan maklumat kuantum yang disimpannya daripada persekitaran ke tahap yang amat tinggi
examples.why: 'persekitaran sekitar' repeats itself, and 'melampau' suggests 'excessive' rather than 'extreme degree'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful overall. The X/Z–CNOT relationships, the inner/outer code roles, degeneracy, and the break-even argument all carry over correctly. [68] renders "Three and a quarter percent or so" as "…peratus atau lebih", which means "or more" rather than "approximately". That is a small, fixable quantity nuance, since the exact value 0.0323 is stated just before. [4] renders the technical term "concatenating" as the generic "menggabungkan" (combining), losing the concept. [62] "mungkin atau tidak mungkin" reads as "possible or impossible", and [29] and [53] have a typo ("diinialisasi") and stiff phrasing ("ketidakpedulian kita yang nampak").

examples.source: Three and a quarter percent or so may not seem like a very good break-even point
examples.translation: Tiga dan satu perempat peratus atau lebih mungkin tidak kelihatan
examples.suggested: Kira-kira tiga suku peratus (sekitar 3.25%) mungkin tidak kelihatan
examples.why: 'atau lebih' means 'or more', which changes an approximation into a lower bound; the source means 'approximately'.

examples.source: the code we obtain by *concatenating* the two codes
examples.translation: dengan *menggabungkan* dua kod
examples.suggested: dengan *merangkaikan* (concatenation) dua kod
examples.why: Concatenation is a specific QEC construction, meaning one code nested inside another. 'menggabungkan' only means 'combine', and [2] already uses it for the looser sense.

examples.source: That may or may not have an effect on the original state
examples.translation: Itu mungkin atau tidak mungkin mempunyai kesan
examples.suggested: Ini mungkin memberi kesan atau mungkin tidak kepada keadaan asal
examples.why: 'tidak mungkin' reads as 'impossible', so this word-for-word rendering of the English is ambiguous in Malay.

examples.source: six initialized workspace qubits
examples.translation: enam qubit ruang kerja yang diinialisasi
examples.suggested: enam qubit ruang kerja yang telah diinisialisasi
examples.why: Misspelling: the correct form is 'diinisialisasi'.

examples.source: This explains our apparent disregard of $Y$ errors up to this point.
examples.translation: Ini menjelaskan ketidakpedulian kita yang nampak terhadap ralat $Y$ sehingga kini.
examples.suggested: Inilah sebabnya kita seolah-olah mengabaikan ralat $Y$ sehingga kini.
examples.why: The phrasing copies English syntax and reads stiffly; a native writer would use a verb construction.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful, and the core terms are used the same way throughout (formalisme penstabil, kod penstabil, boleh cerapan, hasil darab tensor). A native editor would still change three things. In [2], "rangka kerja matematik melaluinya kelas luas…" is missing "yang", so the relative clause reads awkwardly. Also in [2], "seem likely to be well-suited" became "nampaknya sangat sesuai", which drops "likely" and adds "sangat", making the claim a little stronger. In [3], "Ini akan memaklumkan" is a word-for-word copy of the English "inform" and sounds stiff in Malay.

examples.source: a mathematical framework through which a broad class of quantum error correcting codes ... can be specified and analyzed
examples.translation: rangka kerja matematik melaluinya kelas luas kod pembetulan ralat kuantum ... boleh ditentukan dan dianalisis
examples.suggested: rangka kerja matematik yang melaluinya satu kelas luas kod pembetulan ralat kuantum ... boleh ditentukan dan dianalisis
examples.why: Without 'yang' the relative clause is ungrammatical and hard to parse.

examples.source: codes that seem likely to be well-suited to real-world quantum devices
examples.translation: kod yang nampaknya sangat sesuai untuk peranti kuantum dunia sebenar
examples.suggested: kod yang berkemungkinan besar sesuai untuk peranti kuantum dunia sebenar
examples.why: Adding 'sangat' makes the claim a little stronger and drops the 'likely' hedge. A small change that does not mislead.

examples.source: This will both inform and lead into a general discussion of stabilizer codes
examples.translation: Ini akan memaklumkan dan membawa kepada perbincangan umum tentang kod penstabil
examples.suggested: Ini akan menjadi asas dan membawa kita kepada perbincangan umum tentang kod penstabil
examples.why: 'memaklumkan' means 'to notify', so copying 'inform' word for word sounds stiff in Malay.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful and nothing would mislead a learner. Terms like "algoritma pertanyaan kuantum", "pemfaktoran integer" and "Asas Algoritma Kuantum" are correct. A native editor would still fix three small things. First, "search" is "carian" in [0] but "pencarian" in [9]. Second, [9] refers to computers with the pronoun "mereka", which is an anglicism. Third, [17] uses "Penyataan Privasi" where "Pernyataan Privasi" is the usual term.

examples.source: their advantages over classical computers
examples.translation: kelebihan mereka berbanding komputer klasik
examples.suggested: kelebihannya berbanding komputer klasik
examples.why: In Malay, 'mereka' normally refers to people. Using it for computers is a calque of English 'their'.

examples.source: integer factoring and search
examples.translation: pemfaktoran integer dan carian
examples.suggested: pemfaktoran integer dan pencarian
examples.why: Entry [9] renders the same algorithmic concept as 'pencarian (tanpa struktur)'. Using two words for it in one file is inconsistent, and 'pencarian' is the better fit for the algorithmic sense.

examples.source: The IBM Privacy Statement can be viewed here
examples.translation: Penyataan Privasi IBM boleh dilihat
examples.suggested: Pernyataan Privasi IBM boleh dilihat
examples.why: 'Pernyataan Privasi' is the usual Malay term for a privacy statement. 'Penyataan' is mostly used for financial statements.

editor_note: Two passages change the meaning. In [61], "the probability of failure we're willing to tolerate" became "kebarangkalian kegagalan yang kita sanggup tolak", which means "willing to reject". That reverses the trade-off between k and failure probability. "Classical post-processing" is rendered "pemprosesan pascaklasik" ("post-classical processing") in both [23] and the heading [58], which suggests the step goes beyond classical computing, but it is ordinary classical Gaussian elimination. There are also smaller slips: the markup in [22] is broken ("kickback fasa$;m$ qubit"), "In words" is calqued as "Dengan kata-kata" in [54] and [57], "including probabilistic" in [4] became "termasuk kebarangkalian", "XOR eksklusif" in [77] is redundant, and "beberapa kali jalankan bebas" in [23] is ungrammatical.

examples.source: depending on the probability of failure we're willing to tolerate
examples.translation: bergantung pada kebarangkalian kegagalan yang kita sanggup tolak
examples.suggested: bergantung pada kebarangkalian kegagalan yang sanggup kita terima
examples.why: 'tolak' means reject, so the sentence now says the opposite of 'tolerate' and misstates how k relates to the failure probability.

examples.source: followed by a classical post-processing step
examples.translation: diikuti dengan langkah pemprosesan pascaklasik
examples.suggested: diikuti dengan langkah pasca-pemprosesan klasik
examples.why: 'pascaklasik' reads as 'post-classical', which suggests something non-classical. The step is classical post-processing. The same error appears in heading [58].

examples.source: but this time there's no phase kickback; the bottom $m$ qubits all go into the query gate
examples.translation: tetapi kali ini tiada kickback fasa$;m$ qubit di bahagian bawah semuanya masuk
examples.suggested: tetapi kali ini tiada kickback fasa; $m$ qubit di bahagian bawah semuanya masuk
examples.why: The semicolon moved inside the math delimiters, so the page renders ';m' as math and the sentence break is lost.

examples.source: In words, the measurements result in a string ... chosen uniformly at random.
examples.translation: Dengan kata-kata, pengukuran menghasilkan rentetan ... yang dipilih secara seragam rawak.
examples.suggested: Dengan kata lain, pengukuran menghasilkan rentetan ... yang dipilih secara rawak seragam.
examples.why: 'Dengan kata-kata' is a literal calque of 'In words'. The natural Malay phrase is 'Dengan kata lain'.

examples.source: classical (including probabilistic) algorithms
examples.translation: algoritma klasik (termasuk kebarangkalian)
examples.suggested: algoritma klasik (termasuk algoritma berkebarangkalian)
examples.why: This says 'including probability' rather than 'including probabilistic algorithms', which blurs the claim.

editor_note: The four rewritten entries (3, 4, 5, 7) keep the English meaning intact. The caveat "provided that the portion... is large enough" survives as "dengan syarat ... cukup besar", and the terms are used consistently: purification→penulenan, traced out→disurih keluar, fidelity→fideliti, teorem Uhlmann. What's left is phrasing lifted too literally from English. In entry 3, "yang meninggalkan kita dengan $\rho$" copies "leaves us with" word for word. In entry 4, the sentence opens with "Adalah perkara biasa...", which is a common calque of "It's common...". A native technical editor would smooth both, but neither would mislead a learner.

examples.source: a pure state of a larger compound system that leaves us with $\rho$ when the rest of the compound system is traced out
examples.translation: keadaan tulen bagi sistem kompaun yang lebih besar yang meninggalkan kita dengan $\rho$ apabila baki sistem kompaun tersebut disurih keluar
examples.suggested: keadaan tulen bagi sistem kompaun yang lebih besar yang menghasilkan $\rho$ apabila baki sistem kompaun tersebut disurih keluar
examples.why: 'meninggalkan kita dengan' is a word-for-word copy of 'leaves us with'. 'menghasilkan' (or 'memberikan') is how a Malay technical writer would say the partial trace yields rho.

examples.source: It's both common and useful to consider purifications of states when reasoning about them.
examples.translation: Adalah perkara biasa dan berguna untuk mempertimbangkan penulenan keadaan apabila menaakulkannya.
examples.suggested: Mempertimbangkan penulenan sesuatu keadaan semasa menaakul tentangnya merupakan amalan yang lazim dan berguna.
examples.why: Opening with 'Adalah ...' copies English 'It is ...' and reads as translationese. Rewording it around the action as the subject sounds native.

editor_note: Entry 15 is faithful: "Answer" becomes "Jawapan" and "Four." becomes "Empat.", which correctly answers the four-qubit question in [14] ("Berapa banyak qubit dalam litar di bawah?").

The page is faithful and does not mislead: durations, the optional-links caveat and the badge exam steps all match the English. There are three small wording problems. In [6], "anda boleh mengikut pembelajaran mengikut kadar yang anda suka" repeats "mengikut" and reads as a calque. In [7], "mengkaji semula kandungan" means "re-review" where the English only means going through the content. In [17], "untuk bersedia untuk kuantum" doubles "untuk" and is stiff.

examples.source: In this digital course, you can pace your learning however you prefer.
examples.translation: Dalam kursus digital ini, anda boleh mengikut pembelajaran mengikut kadar yang anda suka.
examples.suggested: Dalam kursus digital ini, anda boleh belajar mengikut kadar anda sendiri.
examples.why: "mengikut" appears twice with two different meanings, and the result reads like a calque. A native writer would say "belajar mengikut kadar sendiri".

examples.source: approximately 2–3 hours for reviewing the content directly in this course
examples.translation: lebih kurang 2–3 jam untuk mengkaji semula kandungan secara langsung dalam kursus ini
examples.suggested: lebih kurang 2–3 jam untuk meneliti kandungan secara langsung dalam kursus ini
examples.why: "mengkaji semula" means re-examine or revise, which suggests a second pass. The English means going through the material, so "meneliti" or "membaca" fits better.

examples.source: Identify the steps that you can take to become quantum ready
examples.translation: Mengenal pasti langkah yang boleh anda ambil untuk bersedia untuk kuantum
examples.suggested: Mengenal pasti langkah yang boleh anda ambil untuk menjadi bersedia-kuantum
examples.why: The double "untuk ... untuk" is stiff. Treating "quantum ready" as a set phrase, or writing "bersedia menghadapi era kuantum", reads more naturally.

editor_note: The Malay is faithful and reads naturally, and every condition survives: "sekurang-kurangnya 16 dengan betul untuk lulus" (at least 16 correct to pass), "dikunci sementara" after "dua percubaan" (locked for a while after two attempts), and the whole Credly privacy notice all match the English.

Entry 21, the Credly privacy notice, keeps the English meaning. The data shared (nama, alamat e-mel, lencana), the purposes, the "IBM mungkin berkongsi" hedge and the global third-party sharing all match, so nothing would mislead a reader. "Privacy Statement" is written as "Penyataan Privasi" twice, but the standard Malay word is "Pernyataan Privasi", and a native editor would fix that. The full stop after both links has also moved inside the link text ("[di sini.]"). This is harmless, but it should go back outside the link, as in the English.

examples.source: The IBM Privacy Statement can be viewed [here]... IBM Internal Privacy Statement
examples.translation: Penyataan Privasi IBM boleh dilihat ... Penyataan Privasi Dalaman IBM
examples.suggested: Pernyataan Privasi IBM boleh dilihat ... Pernyataan Privasi Dalaman IBM
examples.why: The standard Malay word for 'statement' here is 'pernyataan'. 'Penyataan' looks like a misspelling.

examples.source: can be viewed [here](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/).
examples.translation: boleh dilihat [di sini.](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/)
examples.suggested: boleh dilihat [di sini](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/).
examples.why: The full stop has moved inside the link text. It should stay outside the link, as in the English.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all through. The 100+ qubit scope, the note that the exam should be taken after the lessons, and the whole Credly privacy notice (e.g. "pemproses data pihak ketiga", "anak syarikat IBM") are rendered correctly, with nothing dropped or inverted. Two phrasings would still be changed by a native editor. In [6], "familiarity with" becomes "kebiasaan dengan", a calque that reads as "habit with", so "biasa dengan" or "pengetahuan asas tentang" is better. In [11], "bertujuan untuk diambil selepas" is a stiff passive calque.

examples.source: we recommend a familiarity with quantum information and quantum circuits
examples.translation: kami mengesyorkan kebiasaan dengan maklumat kuantum dan litar kuantum
examples.suggested: kami mengesyorkan anda sudah biasa dengan maklumat kuantum dan litar kuantum
examples.why: 'kebiasaan' primarily means 'habit/custom'; the calque of 'familiarity with' reads oddly to a Malay reader.

examples.source: This exam is intended to be taken after reading the lessons in this course.
examples.translation: Peperiksaan ini bertujuan untuk diambil selepas membaca pelajaran dalam kursus ini.
examples.suggested: Peperiksaan ini sepatutnya diambil selepas anda membaca pelajaran dalam kursus ini.
examples.why: Literal passive 'bertujuan untuk diambil' is stiff translationese; the meaning is intact.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning, so neither would mislead a learner. Entry 55 correctly says Jordan-Wigner is the common choice, calls Bravyi-Kitaev and parity the more recent encodings, and keeps both bosonic options (Holstein-Primakoff, mapping Fock states to a sub-basis). The one fix needed is in entry 55: "pengekodan fermonik" misspells "fermionik". That is the spelling used in entries 60, 70 and 80, next to "bosonik" in the same sentence. Entry 59's accordion title "Nota pilihan tentang konvensyen" is correct as written.

examples.source: The Bravyi-Kitaev and parity mappings are more recent fermionic encoding.
examples.translation: Pemetaan Bravyi-Kitaev dan pariti adalah pengekodan fermonik yang lebih baru.
examples.suggested: Pemetaan Bravyi-Kitaev dan pariti ialah pengekodan fermionik yang lebih baharu.
examples.why: 'fermonik' misspells 'fermionik'. The correct form is used in entries 60, 70 and 80 and matches 'bosonik' in the same entry. The misspelling does not change the meaning, but a native editor would correct it.

editor_note: The course's core concept, "diagonalization", is translated two ways. Entry [0] uses the correct Malay term, "pepenjuruan". Entries [1] (page title) and [7] use "penepatan", which means "placement" or "fixing" and has nothing to do with matrix diagonalization. That renames the course "quantum placement algorithms", the same kind of wrong domain term as the rubric's variational/permutational example. Minor points: the pronoun switches between "Anda" (entries [0], [6]-[9], [12]) and the lowercase convention "anda" (entry [5]), and in [12] the full stop has moved inside the link text ("[di sini.]").

examples.source: Exam | Quantum diagonalization algorithms
examples.translation: Peperiksaan | Algoritma penepatan kuantum
examples.suggested: Peperiksaan | Algoritma pepenjuruan kuantum
examples.why: 'Penepatan' means placement/fixing, not diagonalization, so the course title names the wrong concept. It also clashes with 'pepenjuruan' in entry [0].

examples.source: ...take the badging exam for Quantum diagonalization algorithms.
examples.translation: ...menduduki peperiksaan lencana untuk Algoritma penepatan kuantum.
examples.suggested: ...menduduki peperiksaan lencana untuk Algoritma pepenjuruan kuantum.
examples.why: The same wrong term again. A learner looking for this badge or course would see a different, meaningless algorithm name.

examples.source: Your feedback will be used...
examples.translation: Maklum balas anda akan digunakan...
examples.suggested: Use one form of the pronoun across the file (the convention is 'anda')
examples.why: Lowercase 'anda' here, but capitalised 'Anda' everywhere else in the file.

editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries (0, 43, 49, 54, 116, 117) would mislead a learner. The fixes are about word choice. In entry 117, 'sparsity' is rendered 'kehampaan', a word that in Malay mostly means disappointment or emptiness. The conventional term is 'kejarangan' (sparse matrix is 'matriks jarang'). Entry 0 uses 'keamatan sumber' for 'resource intensiveness', which is stiff. Entry 49 has the calque 'Ia sering dilihat dipanggil'. Entry 116 uses casual 'kamu' where the convention is 'anda'.

examples.source: the sparsity of the matrices being diagonalized
examples.translation: kehampaan matriks yang didiagonalisasikan
examples.suggested: kejarangan matriks yang didiagonalkan
examples.why: 'Kehampaan' mostly means disappointment or emptiness. The established linear-algebra term for sparsity is 'kejarangan' (matriks jarang).

examples.source: Convergence and resource intensiveness are discussed.
examples.translation: Konvergensi dan keamatan sumber dibincangkan.
examples.suggested: Penumpuan dan keperluan sumber turut dibincangkan.
examples.why: 'Keamatan sumber' is a stiff literal rendering. 'Keperluan sumber' reads more naturally, and 'penumpuan' is the standard Malay term for convergence.

examples.source: One often sees it called a "Krylov subspace"
examples.translation: Ia sering dilihat dipanggil "Krylov subspace"
examples.suggested: Ia sering disebut sebagai "Krylov subspace"
examples.why: 'dilihat dipanggil' is a calque of the English 'sees it called'.

examples.source: if you re-run the calculation
examples.translation: jika kamu menjalankan semula pengiraan
examples.suggested: jika anda menjalankan semula pengiraan
examples.why: The convention is standard 'anda', and casual 'kamu' is a register slip.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The caveats in [54] and [67] and the degree-3 heavy-hex reasoning in [33] all match the English, so a learner would not be misled. There are three terminology slips a native editor would fix. 'Unitary' is rendered as 'kesatuan' (which means union/unity) in [60] and [62], where the conventional term is 'unitari' (matriks unitari). 'Qubit routing' in [33] becomes 'penghala qubit' ('qubit router', a device) instead of 'penghalaan qubit' (the process). 'Pipeline' in [56] is calqued as 'saluran paip' ('water pipe').

examples.source: synthesizing the 2-qubit unitary matrices
examples.translation: menyintesis matriks kesatuan 2-Qubit
examples.suggested: menyintesis matriks unitari 2-Qubit
examples.why: 'Kesatuan' means union/unity. The standard Malay mathematical term for unitary is 'unitari'. The same issue appears in the heading at [60] ('sintesis kesatuan').

examples.source: the original circuit requires qubit routing that adds SWAP gates
examples.translation: Circuit asal memerlukan penghala qubit yang menambah gate SWAP
examples.suggested: Circuit asal memerlukan penghalaan qubit yang menambah gate SWAP
examples.why: 'Penghala' is the agent noun (a router), but the English means the routing process. The correct form is 'penghalaan'.

examples.source: The last default stage in the pipeline is optimization.
examples.translation: Peringkat lalai terakhir dalam saluran paip ialah pengoptimuman.
examples.suggested: Peringkat lalai terakhir dalam aliran (pipeline) transpilasi ialah pengoptimuman.
examples.why: 'Saluran paip' is a literal plumbing calque. The page already uses 'aliran' for the transpiler flow elsewhere, so it would read more naturally and more consistently here too.

editor_note: Entry 47 has the same meaning as the English and would not mislead a learner. It keeps the "rotate before measurement" logic, "make different rotations" and the sdg/API pointer, and its terms (tomografi keadaan kuantum, get, putaran) match the rest of the file. Two small wording problems remain. "mempelajari tentang $r_y$" is redundant: "mempelajari" is already transitive, so "tentang" should go, or it can become "mengetahui $r_y$". "rujuk kepada rujukan API" repeats the root rujuk/rujukan, and "lihat rujukan API" reads more naturally.

examples.source: we can rotate the system prior to measurement to learn about the $r_y$.
examples.translation: kita boleh memutar sistem sebelum pengukuran untuk mempelajari tentang $r_y$.
examples.suggested: kita boleh memutar sistem sebelum pengukuran untuk mengetahui $r_y$.
examples.why: 'mempelajari' is already transitive, so adding 'tentang' is redundant and prescriptively wrong in standard Malay. It reads as a calque of 'learn about'.

examples.source: refer [to the API reference](...)
examples.translation: rujuk [kepada rujukan API.](...)
examples.suggested: lihat [rujukan API](...)
examples.why: 'rujuk kepada rujukan' repeats the same root and sounds clumsy. 'lihat rujukan API' is the natural phrasing and matches entry 97.

editor_note: Faithful, natural Malay throughout. The exam rules keep their meaning ("sekurang-kurangnya 16 soalan", "dalam dua percubaan ... dikunci buat sementara waktu"), and "Reka bentuk algoritma variasi" and "menduduki peperiksaan lencana" are rendered the same way wherever they appear.

The three rewritten entries (0, 6, 11) are faithful and natural. Entry 0 uses "algoritma hibrid klasik-kuantum" and keeps "algoritma variasi" consistent with entry 4. In entry 6, "Peperiksaan ini sepatutnya diambil selepas anda membaca pelajaran" says the same thing as the English. Entry 11 keeps every data-sharing detail and caveat, for example "IBM mungkin berkongsi maklumat peribadi ... dengan anak syarikat IBM dan pihak ketiga di seluruh dunia".

In the results section, entries [84] and [85] translate "magnetization" as "pengewangan", which means "monetization" (from "wang", money). A learner would read "purata pengewangan spin" as "average monetization of the spins", so the plotted quantity is misnamed. Entry [7] correctly uses "magnetisasi", and the conventional term is "pemagnetan" or "magnetisasi". "Classical feedforward" is "suapan ke hadapan" in [4], [9] and [43], but it becomes "suapan balik", "suap balik" or "suapbalik" (feedback) in [30], [72] and [89], which blurs the concept. There are also smaller inconsistencies: "observable" and "boleh cerap" ([78], [84]), "pengukuran pertengahan Circuit" and "pengukuran litar tengah" ([82]), "uniter" and "unitari", the untranslated verb "instantiate" in [52], and a switch from "kita" to "kami" in [89].

examples.source: compute the average magnetization estimated by the observables
examples.translation: kira purata pengewangan yang dianggarkan oleh boleh cerap
examples.suggested: kira purata magnetisasi yang dianggarkan oleh observable
examples.why: 'Pengewangan' means monetization. This is the wrong physical quantity, and it contradicts 'magnetisasi' in [7].

examples.source: we plot the spin magnetization as a function of the Trotter steps
examples.translation: kita plot pengewangan spin sebagai fungsi langkah Trotter
examples.suggested: kita plot magnetisasi spin sebagai fungsi langkah Trotter
examples.why: The quantity in the final plot is misnamed as 'spin monetization'.

examples.source: using ancilla qubits, mid-circuit measurement, and feedforward
examples.translation: menggunakan qubit ancilla, pengukuran pertengahan Circuit, dan suapan balik
examples.suggested: menggunakan qubit ancilla, pengukuran pertengahan Circuit, dan suapan ke hadapan
examples.why: 'Suapan balik' means feedback, not feedforward. It is also inconsistent with 'suapan ke hadapan' in [4], [9] and [43], and the same slip recurs in [72] and [89].

examples.source: we first instantiate the backend
examples.translation: kita mula-mula instantiate Backend
examples.suggested: kita mula-mula mencipta instans Backend
examples.why: The English verb 'instantiate' was left untranslated in the middle of a Malay sentence.

editor_note: Entry 53 renders "Support Vector Machine (SVM)" as the conventional Malay term "Mesin Vektor Sokongan (SVM)", keeps the SVM acronym used in entries 54 and 56, and leaves the heading anchor intact.
